findings.title: Issue #336 local-only PostgreSQL evidence helper accepts driver host override
findings.preconditions: An operator or automated harness provides ISSUE336_PG_ACK=ISOLATED_LOCAL_ONLY and a crafted/misconfigured ISSUE336_PG_URL containing an authority hostname 127.0.0.1, pathname /vaylet336, and a `?host=` query parameter that points elsewhere.
findings.reasoning: WHATWG URL.hostname ignores `host=` search parameter, so the helper's guard accepts the string. Its pg Pool receives the original connectionString and pg-connection-string@2.14.0 copies URL parameters into config (index.js:40-42) and sets the authority hostname only when config.host is absent (index.js:54-56). The query host overrides the checked authority host. This is static guard bypass; no remote connection was attempted.
findings.impact: The claimed isolated-local check does not guarantee the tool connects only to local test PostgreSQL. A nonlocal connection could be attempted using supplied credentials. Real-world remote access and production damage were not demonstrated.
existing_mitigations: Data exercised in BEGIN with CREATE TEMP TABLE/ON COMMIT DROP and ROLLBACK in finally
No permanent target data modification shown by this tool path
findings.next_action: Reject URL.search/hash, unexpected protocols/ports/userinfo constraints as appropriate and verify effective driver connection host is loopback before issuing SQL; add offline parser regression to an authorized follow-up remediation.
findings.dependency_proof: Locked pnpm-lock.yaml resolves pg-connection-string 2.14.0; Prime independently inspected installed 2.14.0 index.js. node-postgres public README specifies query host parameter overrides URI host.

findings.title: Two opt-in matched UI acceptance specs reject normal Dashboard default E2E discovery at module import
findings.trigger_and_preconditions: An engineer runs pnpm --filter @valet/dashboard test:e2e with default environment lacking ISSUE306_VARIANT/ISSUE306_CASE_ONLY and ISSUE314_VARIANT. Playwright loads all *.spec.ts under ./e2e before running tests.

evidence.observation: Top-level require-before-collect checks throw unless a matched before/after variant, E2E_BASE_URL and one case are set. No conditional test.skip guards module evaluation.
Top-level checks throw without ISSUE314_VARIANT and an explicitly localhost E2E_BASE_URL.
test:e2e invokes playwright test without excluding matched baseline specs; test:e2e:runtime uses a separate config.
Current Dashboard CI gate executes test:e2e:runtime with an explicit local URL; the default suite is not shown as a CI blocker.

findings.impact: Ordinary opt-in-free test:e2e collection fails before usable regression assertions can run; normal CI uses the isolated runtime suite, so product runtime impact is not established.
existing_mitigations: The matched baselines deliberately require isolated localhost and explicit before/after provenance when run directly.
The CI E2E step targets ./e2e-runtime, so these import guards do not establish current CI failure.
Tests were not executed in C010; discovery failure is inferred from top-level throw plus standard Playwright file collection.
findings.dedupe_note: Same general category as existing C004-DASH-001 and C006-DASH-001 default E2E suite debt, but these two files have an independent import-time failure trigger. Prime may group them in the existing test-suite debt cluster.
findings.remediation_direction: Keep isolated matched capture guards, but move them into explicit test.skip/fixture-level opt-in execution or a dedicated Playwright project/testDir excluded from the default test:e2e collection. Preserve UI Freeze.

findings.title: Secondary and danger Guest buttons suppress keyboard focus outline
findings.preconditions: Guest uses keyboard Tab to focus an enabled secondary/danger Btn (for example Back or Not now).
findings.consequence: Inline outline:none overrides native focus indicator; app CSS restores focus-visible only for primary/ghost; keyboard user lacks visible indication of focus on affected actions.
findings.existing_mitigations: Primary/ghost brand classes have explicit focus-visible outline, and the native button remains focusable; this does not restore secondary/danger outlines.
findings.limits: Source-supported accessibility defect; physical keyboard/visual browser run not executed. WCAG 2.4.7 focus visible and expected 2.4.11 focus appearance should be verified in supported browsers.
findings.recommendation: Restore a focus-visible outline for secondary/danger variants without changing geometry or semantics; add a browser keyboard-focus regression.

findings.title: Arabic prehydration visibility guard can remain after locale switches to English
findings.preconditions: BeforeInteractive bootstrap sees persisted ar and adds vaylet-persisted-ar. Before React provider resolves client locale, another same-origin tab changes storage preference to en or an equivalent allowed storage change leaves current snapshot en.
findings.consequence: Effect sets html lang=en and dir=ltr but leaves vaylet-persisted-ar because guard removal is conditional on locale===ar; CSS keeps body visibility:hidden until a later Arabic render removes it. Potential blank Customer page in narrow timing window.
findings.existing_mitigations: Arabic-persisted normal hydration removes guard; restricted-storage Arabic fallback is covered by mounted test. Neither covers bootstrap ar followed by current en on first provider effect.
findings.limits: No timing-race browser reproduction was executed; do not count as confirmed runtime defect. Investigate with deterministic hydration/barrier test and real browser cross-tab timing.
findings.recommendation: Make guard removal contingent on hydration readiness regardless of currently selected locale, while retaining protection against English SSR flash for persisted Arabic; verify before changing production behavior.

historical_p1_independent_recheck.audit: C010 W1 targeted historical SEC-011 / GitHub #363 reconciliation
preconditions: Target is an MFA-enabled user with an active ORG_ADMIN or LOCATION_MANAGER membership in an active organization.
A different live, valid password-authenticated StaffAuthSession for the same user already exists or is obtained.
Legitimate user begins self-recovery using a valid one-use recovery code; second session sends enrollment/begin during the replacement PENDING interval.
No prior recovery code, authenticator secret, SQL access or cross-user access is needed by the second session.

current_source_evidence.observation: The recovery session is rechecked; recovery proof is verified and consumed. The ACTIVE factor is retired; a replacement TOTP secret is inserted as an ordinary PENDING factor using only factorId, userId and protectedSecret. No recovery-session/ceremony identifier is persisted.

Enrollment/begin accepts a separate valid session for the same user; after user-level eligibility and lock, a current PENDING factor causes direct unprotectTotpSecret and response provisioning with secretBase32. There is no recovery ceremony or initiating-session comparison.

Enrollment/confirm accepts any same-user valid session with matching PENDING factorId and correct TOTP, activates factor, generates ten recovery codes, calls establishMfaAssurance with that caller's exact session.id, and returns the codes. Neither operation checks which session used the recovery code.
Factor shape and SQL queries constrain userId/state/factorId only, with no session/ceremony ownership field or predicate.

Revalidates the individual access token, user, session lifetime/revocation and management eligibility; locks per user. Establishes assurance on the calling session after TOTP; it never binds the replacement factor to the initiating recovery session.
HTTP enrollment/begin and enrollment/confirm are separate staff bearer operations, while recovery/begin calls the recovery service; no extra controller-level ownership proof.
Bearer resolver requires a valid unrevoked, unexpired StaffAuthSession for an ACTIVE user, but does not require existing MFA assurance for enrollment.
Generic begin accepts an empty object; confirm takes only factorId+TOTP; self-recovery begin consumes a recovery code. There is no recovery ceremony capability in these contracts.

Factor table persists id, user_id, state, protected_secret and replay/recovery metadata, plus one-live-factor-per-user index. No recovery-session owner or ceremony ID. Git grep across migration history found no later MFA ceremony/session-binding migration.

mitigations_and_limitations.existing_controls: ACTIVE factor blocks generic begin; same-user user/advisory and row locks serialize factor changes; valid bearer and management membership required; one-time recovery code is consumed atomically; secret encrypted at rest with userId/factorId AAD; MFA assurance tied to exact session and current ACTIVE factor; other users cannot read this factor.
mitigations_and_limitations.why_not_remediated: None of those controls associates PENDING recovery factor disclosure and confirmation with the session that proved recovery. The second session gets the actual TOTP seed through normal application code, so both encryption and exact-session assurance are subsequently satisfied.
mitigations_and_limitations.proof_gaps: No C010 runtime HTTP/PostgreSQL/model testing. Original model was synthetic, not production exploit proof. GitHub Issue #363 body was inaccessible from this environment; user states it remains open. This report is restricted to pinned d67b source, not mutable remote main.

Require owner-approved recovery ceremony/session binding or equivalent proof capability for both pending secret disclosure and confirmation; preserve explicitly authorized safe retry/resume semantics; add two-session real PostgreSQL/HTTP regression and control cases before resolving issue.
